solution_principle:
5- Graph Mapper: Maps a number of values using a function.

- Practical Example:

- Use the previous Graph Mapper definition.
- Construct a Point.
- Feed the same INPUT range of the Graph Mapper to the X INPUT of the Point.
- Feed the OUTPUT of the Graph Mapper into the Z INPUT of the Point.
- Check the results in Perspective view in Rhino while selecting the Constructed Point.
- Deconstruct the Point to seperate the X,Y & Z values.
- Build a new Circle.
- Construct a new Point and feed its Z with the deconstructed Point above Z value.
- Feed these new Z values into the Plane INPUT of the Circle.
- Feed the X OUTPUT of the Deconstructed Point into the Radius INPUT of the Circle.
- Check the results in Perspective view in Rhino while selecting the Circle.
- Final touch: Loft the circles together.

- If you have a low quality preview of the loft, click on "Preview Mesh Quality" at the Top Right corner of your viewport and select "High Quality".

- Change the type of the Graph Mapper and check out the results!
